records.titleEn: In the gen AI economy, consumers want innovation they can trust
records.evidence:
Our survey finds that most surveyed consumers (53%) are now either experimenting with gen AI or using it regularly—up sharply from 38% in 2024 (figure 1).
1 Overall, tech affordability pressures appear to be easing slightly.
Deloitte Insights and our research centers deliver proprietary research designed to help organizations turn their aspirations into action.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Our survey finds that most surveyed consumers (53%) are now either experimenting with gen AI or using it regularly—up sharply from 38% in 2024 (figure 1).
Gen AI users—those who use it regularly for projects and tasks beyond experimentation—nearly doubled to 20% over the past year.
Roughly half of surveyed gen AI users (51%) say they use it every day, and 38% say they use it at least once a week, which suggests that gen AI is becoming part of their routine digital activities.
Deloitte’s 2025 Connected Consumer survey shows that US households spent an average of US$896 on connected devices in the past year—a significant uptick from US$764 in 2024.
Looking ahead, 29% of respondents say they plan to boost their device spending in the coming year—up threefold from 2023—while 24% say they’re looking to cut back on their device spending (figure 3).
In 2025, about half of respondents (51%) say they expect affordability challenges in the coming year, compared to 61% of respondents in 2024.

Among surveyed consumers, 23% expect to delay device purchases, 17% anticipate not being able to afford the more advanced devices their household wants, and 16% think they may cut back on tech services, subscriptions, or software.
Respondents report that their households spend an average of US$183 monthly on digital services, a slight uptick from US$175 in 2024.

The data suggests this upward trend is likely to continue: A quarter of survey respondents expect to increase their spending on tech services and subscriptions—a sharp jump from 14% who said the same last year.
Another 57% of respondents say they plan to keep their spending steady, down significantly from 72% last year.

Personal use leads gen AI adoption, but work-related use is growing fast Personal use remains the leading application of gen AI, cited by 85% of surveyed users and experimenters, while 22% say they use it for educational or school purposes.
Work-related use (among employed respondents) shows steady growth, climbing from 6% in 2023 to 34% in 2025 (figure 4).
Among those surveyed who are using gen AI for work, more than half (55%) say their organizations encourage its use, and 40% say their companies provide training.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: 68% prioritise AI features in next smartphone, but 82% say trust will decide the purchase: Report AI has overtaken design, price and battery life in purchase priorities, while consumers increasingly demand transparent data practices and on-device AI processing.

A new study by CyberMedia Research (CMR) found that 68% of consumers now prioritise AI capabilities when evaluating smartphones, while 82% said transparent data practices are essential for trusting AI-powered experiences.
The study found that 61% of respondents believe on-device AI processing improves both responsiveness and privacy, indicating growing awareness of how AI functions on smartphones.
Performance remains the most important consideration for smartphone buyers, cited by 78% of respondents, followed by camera quality, including AI enhancements (70%), and AI features (59%).

When choosing between similarly priced devices, 60% of consumers said they prefer a smartphone that offers both strong AI capabilities and powerful hardware, while 25% described themselves as AI-first buyers.
The trend is particularly strong among younger consumers, with 72% of Gen Z respondents saying AI will influence their next smartphone purchase, compared with 65% of millennials.

AI-powered photography continues to be the most widely used application, with 77% of respondents regularly using features such as low-light enhancement, portrait optimisation and intelligent scene detection.
While 66% of female consumers primarily use AI for camera and imaging features, 42% of male respondents prioritise productivity and communication use cases.
CMR also referenced its India Mobile Handset Market Review Report, which found that MediaTek accounted for 47% of smartphone chipset shipments in India.
The survey additionally reported that 93% of MediaTek users expressed satisfaction with their devices, while more than 45% said they would prefer a MediaTek-powered smartphone.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Dentsu Digital survey finds 57% use AI for travel planning

Dentsu Digital launches with AI Lab and publishes a July 2026 survey on consumer AI use in purchasing About one in three private AI users consult AI before purchases, with travel and financial categories above 50% AI use is strongest in awareness, comparison and post-purchase stages, while final buying decisions remain more human-led Dentsu Digital said on July 23 that about one in three consumers who use artificial intelligence in their private lives had consulted AI about purchases made within the past six months, releasing the first findings from a new in-house research unit focused on consumer behavior in the AI era.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Only 45% of marketers gain quality from AI, WARC and TikTok find
by Luis Rijo Luis Rijo Luís Rijo is a seasoned marketing professional with over 10 years of experience in Digital Marketing, Search, Social, Display, Video, and DOOH.

According to the survey, 90% of marketers agree generative AI has become a key tool in the creative development process, 72% use it frequently as a regular part of content production, and 87% believe their organisation is using it effectively for creative development.
WARC's Marketer's Toolkit found that 59% of marketers agree traditional demographic segmentation is no longer effective.
Yet the new survey found demographic data remains the primary input used to brief AI, relied on by 67% of respondents.
Only 17% of marketers make it a rule to always incorporate community or audience insights beyond demographics into generative AI workflows.

Asked to identify the biggest gaps in inputs currently available when briefing generative AI, respondents pointed first to audience behavioural data covering how people engage rather than who they are, cited by 45%.
Access to real-time cultural or community signals and tools that translate insights into effective AI briefs each registered 35%.
Only 10% of respondents said they do not perceive significant gaps in the inputs available to them.

According to the survey, 86% of marketers agree audience behaviour and community signals will influence creative development significantly more over the next three years, and one in three believe access to richer audience or cultural signals would do most to unlock generative AI advantage.

A Taboola study across a publisher network of roughly 600 million daily active users found AI-generated creatives increased or maintained click-through rates without damaging conversion rates , with strongest results in food and drink and personal finance and more muted outcomes in categories such as education.
The WARC and TikTok figure of 87% of marketers believing their organisation uses generative AI effectively sits awkwardly against other industry measurement.
A MiQ survey from November 2025, reported by PPC Land , found 72% of marketers planning AI adoption growth while only 45% felt confident.
The same MIQ Global AI Confidence Curve is cited inside the WARC report itself for a separate finding: only 40% of marketers strongly believe they can apply findings from one campaign to another.
A self-reported 87% effectiveness rating from a vendor-commissioned survey and a 45% confidence rating from an independent one describe the same industry.
Brandwatch survey findings reported in April 2026 identified social listening and consumer research as a top skill gap at 55%, with cross-platform content optimisation at 52%.

The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses

New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.
As previously reported, research has estimated the global disability market to be worth US$13 trillion in annual spending power , making it one of the world’s largest consumer segments.
The report estimates that the disability consumer market is now worth $675 billion, equivalent in size to the global beauty and cosmetics industry.
Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.
Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.
Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.

“The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”
The study found that: Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.
Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

“If the momentum achieved over the past 10 years is any indication of what the future holds, then we can project with confidence that the favourable trends identified in our research will bear brighter tomorrows for the disability community, businesses at large and the US economy overall.”

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Gartner predicts AI models and platforms spend to hit US$64B - ARN

Worldwide end-user spending on AI models and platforms is projected to total US$64 billion in 2026, up 63.4 per cent from US$39 billion in 2025, with more and more enterprises are choosing to work with companies that can provide clear value.

Spending on generative AI (genAI) models is forecast to grow 117 per cent while AI platform spending will rise 36.9 per cent in 2026, according to Gartner’s latest forecast on AI platforms and models. “Enterprise AI budgets are coming under greater scrutiny, with increased focus on usage efficiency, cost control and measurable outcomes ,” said the analyst firm’s senior principal research analyst, Arunasree Cheparthi. “Spending is shifting toward providers who can demonstrate clear value across cost, latency, performance, and reliability. “This is giving an edge to providers that embed evaluation, cost transparency, and usage tracking into customer workflows, making it easier to manage and optimise AI use.” However, as spending becomes more usage-driven, providers face pressure to demonstrate real adoption, sustained use, and durable margins.
This dynamic is accelerating growth in domain-specific language models (DSLMs) and specialised models, which are forecast to grow 210 percent in 2026.

According to Gartner, the AI software market is forecast to grow significantly between 2025 and 2026, with total market revenue increasing from US$39.3 billion to US$64.3 billion, representing 63.4 per cent growth.
The Foundation Generative AI Models segment is expected to more than double, rising from US$11.4 billion in 2025 to US$23.4 billion in 2026, representing a growth rate of 104.2 per cent.
Meanwhile, the fastest-growing segment is DSLMs and specialised genAI models, which is projected to expand from US$1.6 billion to US$4.9 billion, achieving 210.0 per cent growth.

AI application development platforms are forecast to grow from US$6.9 billion to US$9.5 billion (up 38.6 per cent), and AI platforms for data science and machine learning are expected to increase from US$19.4 billion to US$26.4 billion (an increase of 36.3 per cent).

records.titleEn: AI Coding Tools Hit $9B as Pricing Goes Metered
records.evidence:
Coding has become the most contested benchmark in AI, and the tools built on top of frontier models are absorbing real inference costs that a $10 or $20 monthly subscription increasingly cannot cover.
GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.
Enterprise software spent the 2010s moving from perpetual licences to per-seat SaaS subscriptions, another shift driven by vendors needing revenue that tracked usage more closely than a one-time sale ever could.

GitHub moved Copilot onto usage-based billing, charging for premium requests once a plan’s included allowance runs out, at a rate of roughly $0.04 per request under the current schedule.
Copilot Pro still lists at $10 a month and Copilot Enterprise at $39 per user per month, but both now sit on top of a metered layer that tracks actual usage rather than assuming it away.

GitHub’s own research previously found that Copilot users complete tasks about 55% faster than developers coding without it, a strong pitch for adoption but a rough one for margins once millions of developers start running agentic workflows against the same infrastructure.
A flat $20 monthly subscription only works if the average user’s token consumption stays well below what that fee actually covers.
That behaviour is a major reason Claude Code was reported to author close to 4% of all public GitHub commits by early 2026, a figure some analysts expect to pass 20% before the year is out.

Copilot’s installed base remains enormous regardless, with more than 15 million developers across upwards of 77,000 organisations, including a reported 77% of the Fortune 500.

sourceQuantifiedLines.line: Matt Murphy: Inside the $500M Anthropic SPV That Changed Menlo Ventures — BigGo Finance
In early 2024, Matt Murphy walked into a meeting at Anthropic — a pre-revenue AI lab valued north of $4 billion, run by a team that hadn't yet launched a commercial model.
The deal was structurally awkward for Menlo Ventures, a firm that manages roughly $600 million per fund.
That $10 million starter check and the $500 million-plus SPV that followed would become the defining bet of his career.
The SPV itself was Menlo's first, raising over $500 million from limited partners and strategic investors in a process Murphy describes as the single hardest part of the entire deal.
"Never done before, over $500 million, first time," he said.

In applications where user experience directly drives business outcomes — where a 5% improvement in model quality translates to measurable gains in retention and revenue — companies will pay the premium.
Murphy frames it as an inevitable optimization for companies approaching $100 billion in revenue.
Lovable, an AI-first no-code app builder, rocketed from zero to $300 million in annual recurring revenue in roughly a year.
On one end: seed-stage "tracker checks" of $100,000 to $1 million into more than 50 companies per fund.
On the other end: concentrated, later-stage bets above $10 million in ARR, where a company has already emerged as a category leader.
"You're better off being in them at a very small percent than owning a large percent of a company that exits for $300 to $500 million," Murphy said.
Menlo's $3 billion in total fund commitments is calibrated to stay competitive: large enough to write lead checks, small enough to maintain cultural cohesion.

By approach, Proactive IT Services represented around 58.5% of total revenue in 2025 owing to growing adoption of preventive monitoring and predictive maintenance strategies.
In terms of application, Systems & Network Management held nearly 47.8% market share in 2025 as businesses prioritize uninterrupted IT operations across hybrid infrastructure environments.

North America Held 36.5% of the IT Services Market Share in 2025; Asia Pacific Projected to Register the Fastest CAGR Through 2035 In 2025, the North American market is projected to account for around 36.5% of the global market revenue, largely due to high enterprise technology spending and cloud adoption, managed services, and cybersecurity investments across sectors.
